scores.reason: Measure type: post-load multi-sample OGTT (insulin, C-peptide, glucose) plus MR liver fat. The phenotype would choose between intensified and conventional lifestyle programmes, both accepted options (clarification 15). Only the OGTT part is the insulin/C-peptide part; MR fat is not an insulin measure (clarification 27).
sources: PMID 34531293 DOI 10.2337/db21-0526 (medRxiv preprint text, as read by the project)

scores.reason: Limiting assay: immunoassay insulin (and C-peptide), widely available in US labs but not standardised across platforms (clarifications 20, 25). The multi-sample timing and the MR fat step belong to D5. Insulin assay score would also be 2. V31 note: clarification 27 governs (only the insulin part, the immunoassay, is scored; MR fat is not an insulin assay). If clarification 25 were applied to the bundle, D4 would be 1 with the immunoassay (2) in brackets.
scores.correction: V31 skeptic, applied 2026-10-29: which clarification governs stated; score unchanged.

scores.reason: Needs a multi-sample OGTT (several timed draws) plus an MR spectroscopy scan; no routine owner; only research or specialist programmes could do this. Not scored 0 because endocrinology/diabetes prevention programmes could own the decision.
sources: usecases-verified.md row 51 (text: needs multi-sample OGTT and MR fat measure, not routine)

scores.reason: Test burden 3 (about 2 h OGTT with repeated draws, glucose load, low risk); false-result consequence 3 (wrong programme intensity is reversible, low harm). Lower of two = 3.

Default action is the conventional lifestyle programme. Harm of missing a high-risk phenotype is less intensive prevention and delayed progression to diabetes, a moderate delayed harm; the trial outcome was a glucose surrogate, not incident diabetes, so the harm is partly assumed. After V31: scored 1 because no incident-diabetes data exist.
scores.correction: V31 skeptic, applied 2026-10-29: the trial endpoint was a 0.29 mmol/L post-challenge glucose difference and no incident-diabetes data exist, so the harm of a missed high-risk phenotype is largely assumed.

scores.reason: Measure type: fasting-based (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR; one study a mixed composite). The result would decide whether to add metformin or pioglitazone to mood-disorder treatment, choosing among options in a patient already treated; the add-on is off-label for mood disorders, so it does not determine treatment (clarification 15). Whether IR predicts response is untested, which is a D2 issue. After V31: scored 1, as for row 54.

scores.reason: Ordered by a psychiatrist (specialist outpatient) as a fasting blood draw, one step; there is no pathway telling psychiatry to order it. Owner exists, so not 0; fasting draw is a routine lab, but ownership in psychiatry keeps it at 2.

Test burden 4 (fasting venepuncture); false-result consequence 3 (an unneeded metformin or pioglitazone course is reversible; pioglitazone weight gain and oedema are manageable, so it could be 2 for that drug). Lower of two = 3 with metformin as the main case. After V31: test burden 4, false-result consequence 2 for pioglitazone (metformin 3); lower of two = 2.
scores.correction: V31 skeptic, applied 2026-10-29: clarification 17 takes the lower of two scores; the row and Lin's trial include pioglitazone (weight gain, oedema), so the false-result consequence is 2.

scores.reason: Default action is usual mood treatment without an insulin sensitiser. Harm of not adding one is persistent but reversible depressive symptoms, symptomatic and reversible.

Measure type: post-load (INS-30, insulin 30 min after 75 g glucose). The intended decision is low-fat versus low-carbohydrate diet, both accepted options. D1 scores what a valid result would change; the randomised trial found no interaction, which belongs to D2.
sources: PMID 29466592 DOI 10.1001/jama.2018.0245 (project text, skeptic keyword read)

scores.reason: Limiting assay: insulin immunoassay at a timed 30-minute point, widely available, not standardised. Timing is D5.
Would be ordered in specialist or weight-management outpatient care as a two-sample OGTT (baseline and 30 min), which is a short extra protocol; no routine owner in general dietary advice.
Test burden 3 (glucose load, two draws); false-result consequence 4 (either diet gives similar weight loss in the trial, so a wrong assignment is negligible). Lower of two = 3.
sources: usecases-verified.md row 53 (12-month weight change -5.3 vs -6.0 kg)

scores.reason: Default action is either diet by preference. The trial showed no benefit of insulin-guided assignment, so the marginal harm of not measuring is minor (clarification 18).

Measure type: fasting-based (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR); C-peptide in some cohorts. The stated use is prognosis, with a possible metformin or insulin-lowering choice that no trial supports and that is not standard adjuvant care. Prognosis that sets counselling or monitoring is 1 (clarification 11); no accepted treatment option is chosen.
Fasting insulin immunoassay: widely available in US labs, not standardised; cohorts used different insulin assays and HOMA formulas.
Would be ordered by medical oncology or a survivorship clinic (specialist outpatient) as a fasting draw; no pathway, and the result drives no named action.
Test burden 4 (fasting draw); false-result consequence 3 (false reassurance or an unneeded metformin course; possible anxiety, reversible). Lower of two = 3.

Default action is standard adjuvant care without insulin-guided changes. No insulin-guided intervention has shown benefit, so the marginal harm of not measuring is low (recurrence risk exists, but the test does not change an effective action). Named default harm: none from the default itself.
sources: usecases-verified.md row 54 (MA.32 metformin analysis covers metabolic markers, not recurrence)

anchor_issues: Row 51: the use bundles OGTT insulin/C-peptide with MR liver fat; D4 scored on the insulin assay only, MR fat treated as D5 burden (clarifications 25, 27).

Row 52: D1 anchor 2 ('accepted options') is awkward because the sensitiser add-on is off-label for mood disorders; chose 2 on the basis that a clinician would choose among options, not that the option is accepted.
Row 53: a negative entry; D1 scored as the decision the test would inform, not as evidence of no effect (that goes to D2); S scored 0 under clarification 18.
Row 54: prognosis versus treatment selection (clarification 11) chosen as 1 because no treatment selection is supported; D6 'lower of two' gives little discrimination for fasting draws.
assumptions: No searches were run, as the unit instructions allow; all scores rest on the row text in usecases-verified.md, which reports skeptic keyword reads and a preprint text for row 51. I did not open full texts myself.
US setting assumed for D4, D5, D6 and S; US labs run commercial insulin immunoassays without a common standard.
The Row 51 S score assumes a delayed-diabetes harm from less intensive prevention, although the trial outcome was a glucose surrogate.
